content: Ligand 1 is my reference molecule and atom 0 is its pyridine 4-methyl. Continuing the central-ring scan: this episode puts the methyl at C2, the single carbon sitting between the arylamine at C1 and the anilide at C3. That is the position most likely to matter and most likely to fail. On the pyridine ring, substituting either carbon adjacent to a donor or to the ring nitrogen was fatal - C3 dropped to 0.05, C6 to 0.08 - so if the same crowding logic applies to the central ring, a methyl flanked by both N-H groups should collapse activity. If instead it holds or gains, then the central ring's steric requirements are quite different from the pyridine's, which would tell me the two rings sit in different environments rather than in one continuous slot. Everything else is held at its best setting: meta anilide, 4-methylpyridine, cyclopropanecarboxamide, both donors free. Expected product: about 281 Da.
